design_status: Committed before fresh test generation; motivated by historical reader-score distributions and known prior failures.

population_calibration.grouping: Freeze tenant/actor groups from unfiltered training event tool proportions only; never use scenario labels, population labels, actor-name parsing or test tool proportions to assign groups.
population_calibration.method: Within each supported scope, divide rules and sequence scores by their validation q98s, take maximum, divide by that scope's combined validation q98; final threshold is strictly greater than 1.
population_calibration.fallback: For a sparse/zero-scale/missing validation group, use that tenant's pooled validation calibrator only, with at least 50 sessions and positive scales; record fallback. Unknown actors or tenants without a valid reference reject explicitly.
population_calibration.budget: One global floor(0.02 * sessions) cap after candidate selection; no group quotas, component quotas or group-specific review budgets.

mixture: Retain all sessions from whole independent streams with neutral namespaced IDs; use unchanged generator and make_batch implementation. No label-based sampling.
primary: Population-calibrated fusion versus global fusion, rules and sequence on fresh_population_joint; report reader-sequence detected/missed, false alerts and displacement under one shared cap.
promotion_policy: Freeze parameters before generation; report all controls and no test-driven retuning or automatic reference promotion.
limitations: Targeted fresh instances of inspected synthetic families, not blind family validation.
Training-derived behavioral strata are proxies, not authenticated roles or ground-truth populations.
Calibration reuses unlabelled validation for component scaling and within-group thresholds; no guaranteed false-positive rate or fairness guarantee.
Small per-group tails and contaminated validation can produce unstable thresholds and persistent reader misses.
A single queue can displace other populations; there are no per-group quotas.
Profiles are frozen and can become stale after role or policy changes; unknown actors reject, and sparse groups use recorded same-tenant fallback.
Paired intervals hold fitted models and alert decisions fixed; no training/calibration or reranking uncertainty is included.
